title: Systematic review of marine-derived omega-3 fatty acid supplementation effects on leptin, adiponectin, and the leptin-to-adiponectin ratio.
label: Rausch et al. (2021)
intervention: 31 RCTs, varied EPA/DHA doses, populations and duration; searches to June 2018.
endpoint: Leptin, adiponectin and their ratio in blood.
result: 18/31 reported lower leptin or higher adiponectin direction; 9 significant between-group results. Review did not pool effect sizes because distribution/reporting differed.
limitations: Secondary synthesis, not 31 independent confirmations of one formulation. Primary trial overlap retained; dose and population variability preclude universal efficacy.
prior_review: No prior separate appraisal located; prior Wu synthesis covered overlapping trials.
adjudication: Supports recovery of primary trials and limits generalisation; no class-wide admission by vote count.

title: Low-dose fish oil supplementation increases serum adiponectin without affecting inflammatory markers in overweight subjects.
label: Gammelmark et al. (2012)
intervention: 50 overweight adults randomised double-blind to 2 g/day fish oil (1.1 g marine n-3) or 2 g olive oil for 6 weeks; day-1 assessment.
endpoint: Serum adiponectin and adipose/granulocyte fatty-acid incorporation; inflammatory markers.
result: Adiponectin difference +0.55 µg/mL (95% CI 0.02–1.08); adipose n-3 incorporation increased. No overall anti-inflammatory effect.
limitations: Incorporation is not secretion. Mixed EPA/DHA does not isolate EPA versus DHA; small effect, adiposity/clearance mediation unresolved.
prior_review: Not separately appraised before; identifiable in previously retrieved Wu review, not proof of a prior source-level assessment.
final_disposition: support bounded DHA evidence; defer EPA-specific admission
adjudication: Oral delivery is demonstrated for the mixture. Previous blanket missing-delivery wording was too broad; local secretory mediation still unmeasured.

title: Docosahexaenoic acid-enriched canola oil increases adiponectin concentrations: a randomized crossover controlled intervention trial.
label: Baril-Gravel et al. (2015)
intervention: 114 adults with abdominal obesity plus another metabolic-syndrome criterion; five isoenergetic 4-week diet periods with 4-week washouts; oils 60 g/3000 kcal.
endpoint: Plasma adiponectin; inflammatory transcripts in whole blood in subgroup 62.
result: DHA-enriched high-oleic canola oil: +4.5% versus corn/safflower, +6.9% versus flax/safflower.
limitations: Published significant contrasts do not isolate DHA from the high-oleic carrier; no claimed superiority to every canola arm or generic oil/food equivalent.
final_disposition: evidence-only for tested formulation; supports contextual DHA assessment
adjudication: Attributable exposure is the tested oil diet. DHA-specific admission additionally relies on the separate ComparED trial, not this formulation alone.

title: Effect of flaxseed consumption on central obesity, serum lipids, and adiponectin level in overweight or obese women: A randomised controlled clinical trial.
label: Ahmadniay Motlagh et al. (2021)
intervention: 60 women aged 25–50 randomised to balanced diet plus 30 g/day milled brown flaxseed or raw milled rice for 12 weeks.
result: 52 completed (29 flax/23 control). Higher adiponectin between groups; leptin contrast not significant. Weight and waist also changed.
limitations: Differential attrition, complete-case analysis and concurrent weight change; no constituent attribution or proven secretory mechanism. Adiponectin units retained as printed.
adjudication: A defined human food protocol measured an endocrine signal. Admission is limited to studied circulating response, not weight-independent mechanism or universal optimisation.

title: Soluble Fiber Effect on Human Serum Leptin and Adiponectin: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
label: Zeinabi et al. (2023)
intervention: Systematic review/dose-response meta-analysis of soluble-fibre supplementation; searches through December 2021.
result: Overall adiponectin SMD −0.49 (95% CI −1.20,0.21), leptin −0.80 (−1.70,0.08); high heterogeneity.
limitations: Overall null is not proof of no effect. Borderline subgroup signals, heterogeneous preparations and dose modelling do not establish a generic PM8 fibre relationship.
final_disposition: reject general soluble-fibre endocrine claim; retain subtype candidates
adjudication: No generic fibre Type A/B admission; cross-BRS benefits are not PM8 endocrine engagement.

title: Diet-induced weight loss has chronic tissue-specific effects on glucocorticoid metabolism in overweight postmenopausal women.
label: Stomby et al. (2015)
intervention: 49 overweight/obese postmenopausal women, Paleolithic-type versus Nordic-recommendation diet for 24 months.
endpoint: SAT 11β-HSD1 mRNA at 6/24 months; oral-cortisone hepatic conversion and urinary metabolites.
result: Adipose transcript decreased at 6 and 24 months in both groups; hepatic conversion changed transiently. Both groups lost weight.
limitations: Not direct adipose enzyme activity or local cortisol-regeneration flux; diet composition and weight/energy effects not isolated.
prior_review: Already retrieved and appraised in SF13 and prior full-rerun evidence matrix.
final_disposition: admit as qualification of existing dietary-weight-loss SOP
adjudication: Extends the existing programme evidence to a local transcript endpoint without claiming measured regeneration or superiority of a named diet.

title: Dietary macronutrient content alters cortisol metabolism independently of body weight changes in obese men.
label: Stimson et al. (2007)
intervention: Two randomised crossovers: 17 obese men ad libitum for 4 weeks; 6 men isocaloric; high-fat/low-carbohydrate versus moderate fat/carbohydrate.
endpoint: Tracer cortisol turnover, urinary metabolites and SAT 11β-HSD1 mRNA/activity.
result: Systemic cortisol regeneration/inactivation changed; subcutaneous adipose mRNA and activity were unaffected.
limitations: Tissue-specific null bounds this diet protocol; does not exclude all diet effects or contradict different long-term transcript measurements.
prior_review: Already appraised and retained in SF13 and EG1.
final_disposition: no local adipose intervention admission from this result
adjudication: Systemic cortisol changes cannot substitute for adipose target engagement.

title: A randomized, crossover, head-to-head comparison of eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid supplementation to reduce inflammation markers in men and women: the Comparing EPA to DHA (ComparED) Study.
label: Allaire et al. (2016)
intervention: 154 adults randomised in double-blind crossover; 2.7 g/day EPA, 2.7 g/day DHA (90%-pure re-esterified triglyceride supplements), or corn oil for 10 weeks, 9-week washouts.
result: DHA increased adiponectin more than EPA: +3.1% ±1.6% versus −1.2% ±1.7%, P<0.001 in primary abstract; Rausch reports DHA-control contrast.
limitations: No adipose secretion/receptor assay; selected population and supplement form; no ordinary-food, dose-equivalence or clinical benefit inferred.
prior_review: Recovered through mandatory Rausch review; no previous separate appraisal located.
final_disposition: admit DHA Type B for scoped circulating response
adjudication: DHA-specific oral exposure and endocrine signal modulation support the bounded Type B proposition. This is not evidence for tissue secretion or general improvement.

title: Can flaxseed supplementation affect circulating adipokines in adults? An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
label: Abbasi et al. (2023)
intervention: 13 RCTs/15 arms, varied whole/ground flaxseed and oils; searches through December 2022.
result: Pooled adiponectin was not significant; substantial heterogeneity and small-study effects. Whole-flax subgroup differed from oils.
limitations: Secondary synthesis overlaps primary trial. Subgroup findings cannot erase overall uncertainty; no full-class or isolated-ALA effect inferred.
final_disposition: qualifies bounded flaxseed practice; rejects broad efficacy claim
adjudication: Retain positive study and pooled uncertainty together; no duplicate independent replication credit.
